clue.text: Naval officers disciplined lads — about 23?

indicators.note: about means going round something, so the shuffled word wraps another piece
lads who are disciplined are knocked into a new shape, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: 23 is a cross-reference to the answer STAR TURN; its first word points to a star, and Mira is a star in Cetus

explanation.surface: Senior navy men tell off some young sailors about something to do with 23.
explanation.walkthrough: The 23 points to the star half of STAR TURN, so you need a particular star: Mira, the famous variable star, sits inside the reworked LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirals are the highest-ranking commissioned officers in a navy.

clue.text: See Christian member abstain, out to pick up a point?

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters are mixed up
picking something up means adding it to what you already have

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for point

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is urged to refrain, but seems keen to make a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like part of the definition (a bishop's see) but merely invites the reader to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabaptists were members of a Reformation Protestant movement practising adult baptism, so one is a member of a Christian sect.

clue.text: Highly strung female?

parts.note: surface reading: a nervous, excitable woman
setter's reading: a figure literally hung on strings, worked from above, with a feminine ending to its name

explanation.walkthrough: Highly strung usually means tense; read literally it is a puppet dangling on strings, and the French -ette ending makes it female.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet moved by strings from above; the word is a French diminutive of Marion.

clue.text: One hard gentleman stood up as wise man

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: H for hard, as on pencils
a polite address to a gentleman

explanation.surface: A tough gentleman rose to his feet as a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu sage or seer, a holy man of great wisdom.

clue.text: Where horses may be seen — and where cats may be spotted?!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a racecourse just south of Dublin
second meaning, whimsical: a town full of spotted big cats

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the name into leopards and town, and spotted works both as seen and as covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopardstown is a well-known Irish horse-racing venue, and taken literally its name is a home for leopards.

clue.text: Circle not fully presented with a set of books at end of month

indicators.note: placing something at the end of another piece tells you which comes second in the join

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone receives a boxed set of books at the end of the month instead of a full circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic in a mild way: an octant is a part of a circle, not a whole one.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is one eighth of a circle, a sector cut by two radii at forty-five degrees.

clue.text: What's religious in fish? Odd puzzle

indicators.note: something in a fish sits inside the word for that fish

parts.note: a nun is a religious, a member of an order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what holy thing could be inside a fish, an odd puzzle indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' is a noun here, meaning a monk or nun.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a riddle or a difficult problem, so it is a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: See 22
See 23
An item of clothing is on incorrectly — result is rubbing

indicators.note: letters set out incorrectly are in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A garment put on wrongly chafes, leaving a sore patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasion is the wearing or scraping away of a surface by friction, which is what rubbing does.

clue.text: One may take position by river

definitions.text: One may take position by river

indicators.note: one thing next to another, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: an angle is a position or standpoint from which to view something
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Somebody settles down on the bank of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer, while position and river also build it piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is a fisherman with rod and line, who typically sets up on a riverbank.

clue.text: Herb upset lady — was deceitful and wouldn't commit

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A herb upsets a woman who was dishonest and wouldn't commit to a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilly-dally is to dawdle or vacillate, wasting time instead of making a decision.

clue.text: A vast sum British wasted — one country in disgrace

indicators.note: something wasted is lost, so the letter for British is thrown away

parts.note: a bomb is British slang for a lot of money, as in costing a bomb
abbreviation for British, removed from the previous piece

explanation.surface: A country squandering a fortune it had from Britain is shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one B of BOMB goes, leaving BOM. 'Cost a bomb' is British for being very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: An abomination is something loathsome, a thing that is a disgrace or outrage.

clue.text: Flighty types in Paris spend freely

indicators.note: spending freely means letting the letters go loose and rearrange

explanation.surface: Frivolous people splash money about in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty types' suggests fickle people; here it is literal: creatures that fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpipers are wading shorebirds, and birds are things that take flight.

clue.text: Make neat's right somehow for this?

definitions.text: Make neat's right somehow for this?

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy something up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: making neat is what this verb means, and the fodder includes the word neat itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To straighten something is to put it in order or tidy it, which makes it neat.

clue.text: Material in river

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rough woollen cloth
second meaning: the river forming part of the border between England and Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cloth soaking in water; the two halves are separate meanings of one word, linked by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is both a woollen fabric and a river on the Anglo-Scottish border, after which the cloth is said to be named.

clue.text: Feature of many a pub with doubles all round

definitions.text: Feature of many a pub with doubles all round

parts.words: Feature of many a pub with doubles all round
parts.note: surface reading: a pub where everyone is drinking double measures
setter's reading: the ring of double-scoring segments around the outer edge of a target thrown at in a pub game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubles all round' is what a generous drinker orders; on this pub fixture the doubles are the narrow outer ring that scores twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard hangs in many British pubs and has a ring of double-score segments running round its outside.

clue.text: Food shop? Rave about one, becoming wildly excited

indicators.note: about means round, so the second word goes around the single letter

explanation.surface: Someone goes into a delicatessen and gets frantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliriant describes something marked by or producing delirium, a state of wild excitement and confusion.

clue.text: Day you finally classified as 'sodden'

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A wet day is officially recorded as sodden.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturated means soaked through with liquid, just as sodden does.

clue.text: Occupying home, dear princess

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An affectionate word to someone at home, perhaps a royal living there.
explanation.definitionFit: Medea, in Greek myth, was a princess of Colchis, daughter of King Aeetes, who helped Jason.

clue.text: Person's written about Oscar — right hard to understand

indicators.note: is written about here means wrapped around, so one word encloses the rest

parts.note: a being is a person or creature

explanation.surface: A biographer has produced a book on Oscar Wilde, and it is quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests the NATO alphabet letter O, but here it is Wilde the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bewildering is confusing or perplexing, which is to say difficult to make sense of.

clue.text: Old scriptures are held up as a source of inspiration

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means raising it so it reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: Ancient holy texts are revered as inspiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, of lyric and love poetry; a muse is a goddess who inspires artists.

clue.text: Bit of English 'real bad', unlikely to be this?

definitions.text: Bit of English 'real bad', unlikely to be this?

indicators.note: a muddle that is not likely to make sense must be put into order to get the answer
a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here the opening one

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Really poor English writing is not likely to be easy to read.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: badly written English is unlikely to be easy to read, and the letters as given are scrambled, so not readable either.
explanation.definitionFit: Readable means legible or easy and pleasant to read, which bad prose seldom is.

clue.text: Jump and run around in great performance

parts.note: to start is to jump with surprise

indicators.note: turned around suggests the letters are moved about into another order

explanation.surface: A performer leaps and dashes about on stage in a fine show.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main act or outstanding performance in a show.

clue.text: Perhaps crowd in film runs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: background actors making up a crowd scene
second meaning: in cricket, runs not scored off the bat, such as byes and wides

explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like a verb about a film being shown; it is the cricket sense, where runs conceded through byes, leg byes, wides and no-balls are a separate tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are both crowd-scene performers in a film and the cricket runs credited to a batting side without being hit.

clue.text: Like copper maybe, offering final word in nick

indicators.note: one thing set in another, so the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: a dint is a dent or nick
vale is Latin for farewell, a last word

explanation.surface: A police officer gives the last word on arresting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper and nick both suggest police and prison; here copper is the metal and nick is a dent.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper commonly forms compounds with a valency of two, so it is a divalent element in many of them.

clue.text: What's performed by lake with sailors in female attire?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the lake letter is attached alongside
sailors placed in something means they sit inside that word

parts.note: what has been performed is what one did

explanation.surface: A show staged beside a lake has sailors dressed as women.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirndl is a full-skirted dress in the style of Alpine peasant costume, worn by women.

clue.text: A fellow with promises kept, as is right

indicators.note: something kept is held inside, so the promises are enclosed

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man who keeps his word is doing the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like an adjective for proper conduct; it is a noun, a legal entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: An advowson is, in English church law, the right to nominate a priest to a parish living.
